transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this right, and I really don't want you to think badly of me or think I'm crazy. But I'm here because... well, at work—I'm a nursing assistant—I've been having this issue. 

I'm sure it's probably just stress or being overtired, but I keep hearing these voices. They come from the call-light speaker at the desk, and sometimes from the hallway vents. They keep telling me which patient records have been changed. And I know how strange that sounds, I really do, but it's just as clear as somebody standing right next to me. Even when the unit is completely quiet and I know nobody else hears it... 

I'm sorry, does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and answering your question properly.
Do the voices you hear ever tell you to do something, rather than just giving you information?

No, no, they don't do that. I mean, they never tell me to do anything bad or anything like that. I would never listen if they did, I promise you. I take my job very seriously, and I always follow the rules. 

They just... they just tell me things. Like I said, about the records. I just listen, I don't act on it or anything. I hope that's the right answer... I mean, I hope that's what you were asking. I just want to be helpful. Is that what you needed to know?
Are the voices something you hear all the time, or do they come and go?

Well, um... they definitely come and go. It's not all the time at all. I mean, most of my shift I'm just working normally, taking care of my patients, doing everything I'm supposed to do. 

It's usually just... maybe when it's really late, or if I'm particularly tired? I'm pretty sure it's just a fatigue thing. It's not like they're bothering me constantly or keeping me from doing my job well. I'm still a very good worker, I really am. 

So, yes, they just come and go. I hope that makes sense? Did I explain that okay?
Do you find that your mood changes significantly at different times?

Well, um... I guess my mood does change a little bit sometimes. I really hope this doesn't make me sound difficult to work with, because I try so hard to be a good team player. But... some days I just wake up and I feel like I'm finally, truly awake, you know? Like I suddenly have all this clarity and energy, and I feel like I'm meant to go in and just fix everything at work. I just want everything to run perfectly for the patients. 

But the problem is... and I feel terrible admitting this to you... if my husband, or maybe one of the nurses on shift, tells me to slow down or take a breath, I can get a little... well, I snap at them. I don't mean to be mean, I promise. It's just in that moment, I feel like they're blocking something really important that I'm supposed to be doing. 

I always feel awful about it later, because I really hate being rude to people. Is that... does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things the way you need me to.
Do you ever feel like you're not in control when you're in one of those high-energy, clarity moments?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm *not* in control. I'm always very careful to stay in control, especially because of my job. I'd never want you to think I'm running wild or anything like that. 

It's more just... I have so much energy during those times. Like, a really productive amount of energy! I'll work a full shift at the hospital, and instead of being tired, I'll come home and just... keep going. I'll clean the whole house, or I'll sit down and rewrite all my notes so they're perfectly neat, or I'll reorganize all our supplies. 

Sometimes I'll just be pacing around the kitchen, trying to figure out what to fix next, and my husband will be practically begging me to just sit down and rest. But I'm completely in control of it, I'm just... being very thorough. I like to be helpful, you know? It's a good thing to be productive, right? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm out of control. I'm doing okay, aren't I?
Do you ever feel extremely down or sad for periods of time?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. Not extremely down, anyway. I mean, everybody has days where they feel a little tired or... or maybe just quiet, right? But I always try to keep a positive attitude. 

It's so important for my patients to see a smiling face, so I really make sure I don't let myself get sad like that. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm, you know, a gloomy person or not capable of doing my job with a good attitude. I try my absolute best to be cheerful for everyone around me. 

I'm a very positive person, mostly. Is that... is that okay to say? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever had a period where you felt sad or empty for most of the day?

Oh, um... empty? No, I don't think I've ever felt empty. I mean, sometimes I get a little worn out, just physically tired from being on my feet at the hospital all day. But not sad or... or empty for the whole day. 

I have so much to be grateful for, you know? My husband, my job... I always try to count my blessings. I really believe that if you just keep busy and keep a smile on your face, you don't really have time to sit around feeling sad. I just focus on being there for my patients and my family. 

I hope that's okay to say? I just... I wouldn't want you to think I'm hiding anything from you, I promise I'm not. I just really try to be a happy person. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a time when you lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I ever lose interest in things. I mean, I love my hobbies. I love baking for the nurses' station and taking care of my garden. 

Sometimes, if I've been working a lot of overtime, I might not have the energy to get out in the yard on my day off. But that's just because I'm being responsible and resting my body so I can be at my best for my patients the next day. It's not that I don't *want* to do those things, I just... I prioritize my responsibilities, you know? 

I always try to stay engaged and keep up with my interests. I think it's so important to have a well-rounded life. I wouldn't want to be someone who just gives up on the things they love. That sounds awful, doesn't it? I really do try to stay active and involved in everything I enjoy. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you ever feel extremely happy or elated for periods of time?

Well, um... happy? Yes, I suppose I do have days where I feel very happy. I mean, it's a good thing to be happy, right? 

Sometimes I wake up and I just feel... like I'm finally fully awake, you know? Like I have all this wonderful energy and I'm meant to go into the hospital and just... fix everything. Organize the supply closets, cheer up all the patients, just make everything perfect. It feels really good to be that helpful. 

But, um... sometimes, if my husband or one of the charge nurses tells me to slow down or take a break... I guess I can get a little, well, snappy. I don't mean to! I just feel like they're getting in the way of something really important I'm supposed to be doing. I always apologize afterward, of course. I hate being sharp with people. 

Is it... is it bad that I get a little irritable when I'm trying to help? I just get so focused on doing a good job. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a difficult person to work with...
Do you feel like these really energetic and productive times are separate from your normal self, or are they just a part of who you are all the time?

Oh, um... well, I like to think it's just me, you know? Just me having a really good day where I'm finally living up to my potential. 

I mean, everyone has days where they're more productive than others, don't they? I just... I really want to be the best nursing assistant I can be, and the best wife. So when I have those days with all that energy, I just feel like I'm finally doing what I'm supposed to do. Like I'm finally getting it right. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm some sort of Jekyll and Hyde person, because I'm really not. I'm always just... me. Just trying to be helpful and do a good job. It's just that sometimes I have a little more pep in my step. That's a normal thing, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
Do you ever do things during those highly energetic times that you later regret?

Oh, um... regret? No, I really don't think so. I mean, I try very hard to always be a good person, you know? 

Like I was saying, I mostly just use that extra energy to work harder at the hospital or get things done around the house. I wouldn't do anything... well, anything bad or reckless, if that's what you're asking. I take my responsibilities as a wife and a nursing assistant very, very seriously. 

I suppose sometimes I might stay up a little too late scrubbing the kitchen or baking, and then maybe I'm a bit physically tired the next day, but... that's not really something to regret, is it? Because it's all for a good cause. I just want to be helpful and do things right. 

I hope that makes sense. I'd hate for you to think I was out doing irresponsible things or making a mess of my life. I really do try my best to be reliable. Is... is that what you meant?
Do you feel like these energetic and productive times happen in cycles, or are they more random?

Cycles? Um, well... I'm not entirely sure what you mean by that. I don't think I've really noticed a pattern or anything like that. 

I think it's mostly just random, you know? Like, sometimes I'll just wake up and feel really good and ready to take on the day. Maybe the sun is shining, or I know it's going to be a busy shift at the hospital and they really need me. It just... happens when it happens, I guess. 

I wouldn't say it's like a clockwork thing or anything that I can predict. I just try to make the most of those good days when they come around. That's the right way to handle it, don't you think? Just... being grateful for the energy when it's there? I hope I'm explaining this okay... I just haven't really kept track of it like that.
Do you feel like your mood is particularly high or elevated when you're having those very energetic and productive times?

High? Um... well, I guess I'd say I just feel... really awake. Like my eyes are finally open and I'm just meant to go in and fix everything at work that needs fixing. It's a wonderful feeling, honestly, because I'm able to be so helpful to everyone. 

Though, I suppose... well, sometimes if I'm in the middle of getting all those important things done, and my husband or maybe one of the charge nurses tells me I need to slow down... I might get a tiny bit frustrated? I might snap at them just a little bit. Not because I'm a mean person! I would never want you to think that. It's just... it feels like they're blocking something really important that I'm supposed to be doing, you know? 

I always feel terrible if I'm short with anyone, and I really don't mean to be rude. It's just that I'm trying so hard to do a good job for the patients and my family. That's understandable, isn't it? I just get a little too focused on helping.
Have you ever felt sad or depressed for two weeks or more?

Sad? Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. Not for two whole weeks, definitely not. I mean, everyone has a bad day here and there, right? 

Sometimes if I'm just very tired after working a lot of shifts, I might feel a little quiet or want to rest, but I wouldn't call that being depressed. I always make sure to get up and take care of my husband and go to my job. I would never just stay in bed and let people down like that. I know how important it is to be dependable. 

I try to keep a very positive attitude, you know? I think it's so important to just smile and push through things. I really hope you don't think I'm the sort of person who just gives up or wallows in things. I try very hard to be strong and keep going. That's the best way to handle things, isn't it? Just keeping your chin up?
Do you feel like you're always in a good mood, even on days when you're not feeling extremely energetic?

Always in a good mood? Oh, well... I try my best to be! I really do think a smile goes a long way, especially working with the patients. But, um, I wouldn't say I'm *always* in a perfect mood. I mean, nobody's perfect, right? 

Sometimes if it's just a regular day and I'm not feeling that... that big burst of energy, I might just feel, well, normal. Or maybe a little quiet. Just an average day, I guess. If I'm a little worn out from my shifts, I might not be practically humming with happiness, but I try very hard not to let it show. I would never want to bring anyone else down just because I'm having a quiet day. 

I think it's just so important to keep things pleasant for everyone else, you know? Even if you're just feeling okay, you should still put your best foot forward. That's the right way to be, don't you think? Just trying to be a positive person for the people around you?
Do you ever do things without thinking them through when you're feeling extremely energetic and productive?

Without thinking them through? Oh, um... no, I really don't think I do that. I try to be a very responsible person, you know? 

Especially at work—being a nursing assistant, you really have to pay attention to what you're doing. You can't just... act on a whim. So even when I have all that wonderful energy and I'm getting so much done, I'm doing it because I see a problem and I know exactly how to fix it. It's not like I'm just being reckless. I would never want to be careless, especially not with the patients or with my family. 

I always try to make sure I'm doing the right thing. It's so important to be dependable and think things through, don't you agree? I really hope you don't think I'm the sort of person who just acts wild or irresponsible. I just try to use my energy to be as helpful and productive as possible.
When you're having one of those very energetic and productive times, do you find that you need less sleep than usual?

Less sleep? Oh, well... I suppose I might sleep a little bit less, but not in a bad way! It's not like I'm tossing and turning or struggling with insomnia. I hate the idea of wasting time in bed when there's so much good work to be done. 

When I have all that wonderful energy, I just... I wake up feeling so refreshed and ready to go, even if it's only been a few hours. I feel completely rested, I really do. It's actually quite nice because it gives me extra time to get things ready for my husband or maybe pick up an extra shift at the hospital. They're always so short-staffed, and I like to be the one they can rely on. 

I don't think it's a problem to need a little less sleep if you're still functioning perfectly well and helping people, right? It just means I'm making the most of my day. That's a good thing, isn't it?
Do you tend to spend more money than usual when you're feeling extremely energetic and productive?

Spend more money? Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I'm very careful with our finances. My husband works so hard, and I would never want to be wasteful, you know? 

Sometimes, if I'm feeling especially good and I've picked up some extra shifts, I might... well, I might buy a little something nice for the house, or maybe a small gift for my husband. Just to show I appreciate him. Or maybe bring some nice treats in for the nurses on the floor, because they work so hard and it cheers everyone up. 

But it's never anything extravagant or silly. It's just being generous, I think. There's nothing wrong with wanting to do nice things for other people when you're feeling blessed with a bit of extra energy and a little extra paycheck, is there? I always make sure the bills are paid first. I'm a very responsible person, I promise you that.
Do you feel like you're a different person when you're having those extremely energetic and productive times?

A different person? Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean... I'm still me, you know? Just... maybe the best version of me. 

I think everyone has times when they feel a bit more upbeat or capable, don't they? When I have that energy, I just feel like I'm finally able to be the wife and the worker that I'm supposed to be. I'm just more helpful, more focused. I don't feel like a stranger to myself or anything frightening like that. 

I would hate for you to think I turn into someone else, someone unrecognizable. I'm just... I'm just getting things done and trying to be a good person. That's perfectly normal, right? To just feel like you're operating at your full potential sometimes?
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy, irritable, or had a lot of energy that lasted for several days or more?

Extremely happy or irritable? Well... I wouldn't say "extremely," no. That makes it sound so... out of control. But I suppose there are days—sometimes a few days in a row—where I just feel... awake. Like I'm finally meant to step up and fix everything at work, you know? Like I can just see exactly what needs to be done on the floor and I have the energy to do it. 

It's a wonderful feeling, really, being that capable. But... well, I suppose I do get a tiny bit frustrated sometimes. If my husband tells me I need to sit down and rest, or if one of the other nurses tells me to slow down when I'm just trying to help... I might snap at them a little bit. It's just because I feel like they're blocking something important that I'm supposed to be doing, and I don't want to lose my momentum. 

I always apologize afterward, of course. I don't like being sharp with people. It's just that I get so focused on doing a good job. That's understandable, isn't it? To get a little testy when people interrupt your work?
